title: A Slice-Rank Drift Bound for Random Quantum \(k\)-SAT
abstract: Random quantum satisfiability is a natural quantum analogue of random constraint satisfaction and a basic model for frustration-free local Hamiltonians. Despite extensive work on its satisfiable and unsatisfiable regimes, the quantitative location of the random quantum \(k\)-SAT threshold has remained poorly understood, with the best general upper bounds leaving a large gap to the known lower bounds. In this paper we prove a new upper bound on the satisfiability threshold of random quantum \(k\)-SAT. Our result improves the previously known asymptotic upper bound by a factor of order \(k\), giving a bound of order \(2^k/k\). The improvement is also significant at small values of \(k\); in particular, for random quantum \(3\)-SAT we obtain a substantially smaller explicit upper bound than the one previously available. The proof combines the geometric formulation of generic quantum satisfiability with a dimension-decay analysis of the full satisfying subspace. The key input is a multiplicative Shearer-type inequality for tensor-product subspaces, which quantifies how global dimension forces nontrivial local dimension on typical sets of qubits.
summary: This paper tackles the hard problem of finding the threshold where random quantum k-SAT instances transition from being satisfiable to unsatisfiable. By developing a dimension-decay analysis using advanced tensor methods, the authors derive a significantly improved upper bound for this critical threshold, $\alpha_{\star}(k) \sim 2^k/k$. This provides crucial quantitative insight into the physics of highly constrained quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is determining the quantitative location of the satisfiability threshold for random quantum k-SAT instances.
main_result: The authors establish a new upper bound on this threshold, showing it scales as $2^k/k$, significantly improving previous asymptotic estimates.
method: The proof combines geometric formulation with a dimension-decay analysis of the satisfying subspace, utilizing a multiplicative Shearer-type inequality for tensor-product subspaces.
model_or_system: The model is random quantum k-SAT, which serves as a quantum analogue to classical constraint satisfaction problems and models frustration-free local Hamiltonians. Satisfiability requires finding a non-zero state in the kernel of the local Hamiltonian projectors.
key_observables: Dimension of the satisfying subspace ($S$), satisfiability threshold ($\alpha_c(k)$), and contraction ranks ($r_T(W)$).
important_parameters: The constraint size $k$, the number of constraints relative to system size ($m/n = \alpha$), and the critical density $\alpha_{\star}(k)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the 'generic' nature of the random local constraints, meaning results hold outside sets of measure zero.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the problem (quantum k-SAT threshold) to developing key mathematical tools (Shearer-type inequality, dimension drop lemma), and finally applying a stopped martingale/drift analysis to derive the asymptotic bound $\alpha_{\star}(k)$.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical bounds on the complexity of quantum constraint satisfaction problems, which are central to understanding ground states in frustrated quantum many-body systems.
